cards.body:
## Summary
Make 'where the slip is' a rule in lib/rules/maths, computed on the server from the learner's own lines, instead of a guess the Lamplight TV module makes from prose. rootOf(question) finds the linear root in code; locate(question, lines) returns the first working line the root stops satisfying, and a sign kind only when exactly one sign flip repairs it. Marking and settling write that into PracticeItem.slipAt, the contract the store already keeps and nothing fills.

## Description
Today the paper's pen has three steps (working.ts): slipAt, which nothing produces (0 producers); a line ordinal parsed out of the rulebook's prose `points` (3 of 12 slips, the same line for every learner, with the lines before it ticked); else the answer line (the other 9). The design law the owner chose says the opposite: no guessed positions, ticks earned. The data to do it right is already on the server at marking: the question, the learner's transcribed working, and verify.ts's evaluate(). The move: (1) rules/maths gains workingLines (moved from working.ts, so server and TV index the same lines), rootOf (two evaluations, a third to prove linearity, null otherwise) and locate (first line that fails at the root; a sign mark only when one term's flip repairs it and never on a line where x stands alone, so the answer's own sign is never ringed); (2) mark.ts asks for the working one step per line and sets slipAt on every wrong item; explain's settle does the same through practice.settle; (3) working.ts stops parsing prose - it draws slipAt, else marks the answer line with no ticks - and a pure lookAt() makes the taped card agree with the pen; (4) Slip gains `name`, and MathsTV's hand-kept SLIP_NAME table goes. The verdict logic in mark.ts is untouched (GUARD in case 6): only where the pen goes changes.

## Flow
- phone sends the worked sheet -> /api/mark -> vision reads working one step per line -> verify decides the verdict as today
- wrong item -> rules/maths locate(question, workingLines(item)) -> slipAt {line, span?, kind?} -> practice.marked -> store keeps it
- Walk: working.ts draws the ring on '- 7' in line 0, ticks nothing after it, the card says 'Look where the pen is.'
- unsure item explained -> settle wrong -> same locate -> practice.settle carries slipAt
- no readable line, or no linear root -> no slipAt -> the answer line is marked, nothing ticked, nothing guessed

## Expected impact
Every wrong item with transcribed working gets its pen on the line where the maths actually broke, and a ringed sign where one flip is the whole mistake - the Lamplight review page's headline promise becomes true in production. Ticks stop being claimed for lines the desk never checked. The pen decision leaves the client TV module for lib/rules (repo law: decisions stay in code), the line split becomes one rule shared by server and screen, and the slip names stop being kept twice.

## Evaluation
Claim: the slip position is decided once, in rules/maths, from the learner's lines and a code-found root; the TV only draws it; no prose ordinal places a pen or earns a tick; no answer sign is ever ringed.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (0 producers of slipAt; 3 of 12 slips placed by a fixed ordinal; 12 slip names kept twice)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/maths-rules-test.cjs and tools/maths-type-test.cjs, engines stubbed at engine.text / engine.vision as those suites already do
Result: better
Gate: contract

cards.body:
## Summary
Make Essay Master's 'Rewrite on my phone' a real loop: the phone opens the sentence on screen, prefilled; the desk re-judges that one sentence in its paragraph through the same lens; the TV stays on it, the rail arrow turns, and the move inks only when the rewrite actually holds. Today the ink is drawn the moment the button is pressed.

## Description
The forensic page teaches one move for one sentence, then asks the learner to leave it: Rewrite posts a status line (keys.ts:280), the phone's Essay tab holds a local sample paragraph (page.tsx:37), the learner must find the sentence, edit it inside the whole paragraph, check the lens radio, and send - which re-judges every sentence (essay.ts:32), records a new paragraph read (essay.ts:57-64), and drops the TV back on the first faulty sentence (store.ts:235) with the old reading gone. Meanwhile the move was already inked when they pressed the button (EssayTV.tsx:280 -> css :162). The leap: rules/essay gains revise(reading, n, text) - one sentence in, one out, numbering and stats recomputed in code, identical/blank/split rewrites refused before any model call - and rewriteState(verdict) -> none | holds | still. desk/essay.ts gains reviseSentence: the model judges sentence n alone, in context, against the move it was taught; the verdicts of every other sentence are kept by code, not by asking. POST /api/analyse {kind:'rewrite'} runs it as the analyse job keyed 'sentence:n' and lands essay.revised (server-only), which keeps essayAt on n. The phone's Essay panel, while the TV is on the forensic page, shows 'Sentence n' with its text and one Send. The TV inks the move only on 'holds', and the rail draws the sentence's old arrow as a faint ghost beside the new one - the before/after is a picture, the caption slot keeps its one sentence.

## Flow
- TV forensic, sentence 4 faulty, move hatched -> Rewrite on my phone (status line, as today)
- phone Essay panel: 'Sentence 4' prefilled with the learner's own sentence -> edit -> Send
- /api/analyse {kind:'rewrite', n:4} -> revise() checks one sentence, not identical -> reviseSentence judges sentence 4 only -> essay.revised
- TV stays on sentence 4: arrow turns forward if it holds, ghost of the old arrow behind it, the move inks; still faulty -> stays hatched, the caption says why
- no writing episode, no lens attempt: the paragraph was read once

## Expected impact
The fix-one-sentence loop goes from ~8 steps across two devices with a blind edit (find the sentence in a textarea that may not hold this paragraph) to 3, with the answer on the sentence the learner was looking at. Untouched sentences can no longer flip verdict, the lens record stops counting a one-sentence fix as a new paragraph, and the one piece of ink on the page stops lying. Withholding is intact: the only sentence ever shown is the learner's own.

## Evaluation
Claim: a rewrite of sentence n changes only sentence n's text and verdict, is refused in code before any model call when it is not one new sentence, keeps the TV on n, writes nothing to the learner record, and the move is inked only when the rewrite holds.
Before: 0 of 7 new acceptance cases pass (plus 1 GUARD green before by design); ink drawn on button press in 1 of 1 rewrite paths
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/essay-rules-test.cjs and tools/desk-jobs-rules-test.cjs, engine.text stubbed as essay-rules-test already does; no live model call
Result: better
Gate: contract
